top_signals.summary: For the first time since 2009, the Conference of the Parties ended without a deal to advance an energy transition as participating countries failed to agree on key aspects of that deal. Disagreements were most notable in financial commitments for developing countries and in blaming oil and gas for climate change. COP31 was arguably doomed from the start. top_signals.title: EIA forecasts Alaskan crude oil production to grow 13% in 2027
top_signals.summary: After decades of decline, crude oil production in Alaska is growing, driven by two projects on Alaska's North Slope. In our latest Short-Term Energy Outlook, we expect a 23,000 barrels per day (b/d) (6%) increase in 2026, followed by a 60,000 b/d (13%) rise in 2027. At a forecast 505,000 b/d in 2027, output would be the most since 2014.
